_meta.indication: SYMPROIC is indicated for the treatment of opioid-induced constipation (OIC) in adult patients with chronic non-cancer pain.

pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with opioid-induced constipation (OIC) and chronic non-cancer pain on a stable opioid regimen
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Difference in proportion of responders, where a responder had at least 3 SBMs per week and a change from baseline of at least 1 SBM per week for at least 9 out of the 12 study weeks and 3 out of the last 4 weeks
pivotal_trials.result: Responders 130 (48%) SYMPROIC vs 94 (35%) placebo; treatment difference 13% [95% CI 5%, 21%]; p value 0.0020

pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with opioid-induced constipation (OIC) and chronic non-cancer pain on a stable opioid regimen
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Difference in proportion of responders, where a responder had at least 3 SBMs per week and a change from baseline of at least 1 SBM per week for at least 9 out of the 12 study weeks and 3 out of the last 4 weeks
pivotal_trials.result: Responders 145 (53%) SYMPROIC vs 92 (34%) placebo; treatment difference 19% [95% CI 11%, 27%]; p value <.0001

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=2%) are abdominal pain, diarrhea, and nausea. In pooled Studies 1 and 2: abdominal pain 8% vs 2% placebo, diarrhea 7% vs 2%, nausea 4% vs 2%. Opioid withdrawal occurred in ~1% of subjects. GI perforation and opioid withdrawal are warnings.
target_moa: Naldemedine is an opioid antagonist with binding affinities for mu-, delta-, and kappa-opioid receptors that functions as a peripherally-acting mu-opioid receptor antagonist (PAMORA) in tissues such as the GI tract, decreasing the constipating effects of opioids.
modality: Small molecule (oral opioid antagonist; derivative of naltrexone)

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened to discuss this application because it did not raise significant public health questions and outside expertise was not necessary.

basis.text: The application was reviewed under Standard (not Priority) review.

summary.text: Naldemedine (Symproic), a new molecular entity and PAMORA derivative of naltrexone, received a standard-review NDA approval on the PDUFA goal date based on two replicate 12-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials (V9231, V9232); no advisory committee was convened for this application, and a MACE post-marketing observational study was required.

citations.quote: Naldemedine, a new molecular entity, is a derivative of naltrexone. It is an antagonist of opioid binding to mu-, delta-, and kappa-opioid receptors.
The FDA reviewers found that two randomized, controlled clinical trials submitted to the NDA (Study V9231 and Study V9232) supported nalmedemine's approval for the proposed indication. I concur.

There was no advisory committee convened to discuss this application because the application did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the drug in the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of a disease and outside expertise was not necessary.

requirement.text: PMR 3174-1: A post-marketing observational epidemiologic study comparing Symproic to other OIC treatments in patients with chronic non-cancer pain, with a primary composite outcome of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: CV death, nonfatal MI, and nonfatal stroke).

citations.quote: 3174-1 A post-marketing, observational epidemiologic study comparing Symproic (nalmedemine) to other treatments of opioid induced constipation in patients with chronic non-cancer pain. The study's primary outcome is a composite of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE): cardiovascular (CV) death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and nonfatal stroke.
